title: The 5 Highest Mountains on Earth, Ranked (#1 Isn't the Tallest)

scenes.text: The five highest mountains on Earth, ranked. Number one is not even the tallest mountain on the planet.

scenes.label: Makalu · 8,485 m
scenes.text: Number five: Makalu. Eight thousand four hundred and eighty-five meters, with a sharp four-sided pyramid summit.

scenes.label: Lhotse · 8,516 m
scenes.text: Number four: Lhotse. Eight thousand five hundred and sixteen meters, joined to Everest by a high ridge called the South Col.

scenes.label: Kangchenjunga · 8,586 m
scenes.text: Number three: Kangchenjunga. Eight thousand five hundred and eighty-six meters, on the border between Nepal and India.

scenes.label: K2 · 8,611 m
scenes.text: Number two: K2. Eight thousand six hundred and eleven meters, just two hundred and thirty-eight short of the top.

scenes.label: Everest · 8,849 m
scenes.text: Number one: Everest. Eight thousand eight hundred and forty-nine meters above sea level, though Mauna Kea is taller from its base.

description:
The five highest mountains on Earth, ranked by height above sea level.
From Makalu to Everest, which tops the list even though Hawaii's Mauna Kea is taller measured from its base on the ocean floor.
Which of these peaks would you dare to climb?
first_comment: Which of these peaks would you climb first? And what should we rank next?
